subject: ACME POC: eval methodology & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya (cc'd),

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment overall. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC:

- Success criteria (proposal):
  - Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms for typical customer queries (sample set attached).
  - Accuracy: end-user satisfaction >= 85% on prioritized intents (measured by blind annotation).
  - Cost: target RL cost <= $0.XX/token (we'll refine once we see trace).
- Evaluation plan:
  - Offline evals: run our rubric-driven batch evaluation on your historical dataset (we'll need a sanitized sample).
  - Online shadow: run a 2-week shadow mode for top 5 routes to measure production signal and latency.
- Ownership / timeline:
  - Redwood: run offline evals, provide rubric and baseline results (Marissa / Dylan).
  - ACME: provide 1-2 weeks of sanitized historical logs + a list of priority intents (Alex / Priya).
  - Proposed timeline: kickoff next Monday 5/10, offline results by 5/17, shadow 5/18–5/31.
- Next immediate actions:
  1) Alex/ACME: share sample logs and confirm priority intents.
  2) Redwood: send draft eval rubric and a POC success criteria doc (attached).

Attachments: ACME_POC_eval_plan_v1.xlsx (proposed timeline + milestones)

If that looks right, I'll kick off the internal eval run and schedule a short sync for 5/17 to review results.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A few quick notes/questions from our side:

- We can provide a 2-week window of historical queries (anonymized) by Friday 5/7. Will that be enough for the offline runs?
- For accuracy targets: 85% sounds reasonable as a starting point. Can the rubric include intent-level pass/fail and graded correctness (0/1/2)?
- On shadowing: we prefer a non-blocking shadow (no writes) for the first phase. We'll also want to log any mismatches to a shared S3 for inspection.

I'll get the logs to you and Priya will confirm the priority intents list. One ask — can Redwood provide a short example rubric before 5/7 so we can sanity-check?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: post-call recap & next steps

Great — thanks Alex. Yes, 2 weeks of anonymized logs is perfect for the initial offline pass.

I've attached a short draft rubric (eval_rubric_draft.md) and included a high-level description here:

- Grading scale: 0 = incorrect/harmful, 1 = partially correct, 2 = fully correct / acceptable.
- Intent-level pass: average grade >= 1.5 across the sample for that intent.
- Aggregate pass: weighted average across priority intents >= 1.6 AND manual sample rate (random 200 responses) with >= 85% acceptable.

We'll run the offline batch with your sample and return a report with per-intent breakdown, failure cases, and suggested prompt/system tweaks. After that, we'll propose a 2-week shadow window for production validation.

Action items updated:
- ACME (Alex/Priya): share sanitized logs + intents by 5/7.
- Redwood (Marissa/Dylan): run offline eval and send results by 5/17; share rubric link in prior to 5/7.

Attaching draft rubric: eval_rubric_draft.md (Markdown, 6KB)

Thanks,

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Priya / team — quick reply from engineering ops side.

- Tracing: yes — we can provide per-request traces including token-level timings, model variant, and routing decisions. We'll redact any PII from logs before sharing.
- Escalation: please loop in me (dylan.brooks@redwood.com) for any infra/perf regressions and Rachel Kim (rachel.kim@redwood.com) for evaluation/quality questions. For executive escalation, Marissa will coordinate with Sales/CS.
- On grading rubric: we'll add a complementary "online mismatch" metric for shadow results: percentage of requests where Redwood answer differs materially from current production routing + severity tag (low/medium/high).

I'll schedule a 30-min aligner for 5/17 to review offline results and define the shadow instrumentation. Proposed attendees: Marissa, Dylan (Redwood); Alex, Priya (ACME).

Thanks — looking forward to it.
